#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -c 1 -g 1 -t 2h --setattr=system.memory=17408M --job-name=brats --output=logs/test_brats.txt script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from --nodes=1)
# -n 4         : 4 tasks (from --ntasks-per-node=4)
# -c 1         : 1 core per task (implicit, default)
# -g 1         : 1 GPU (from --gres=gpu:1)
# -t 2h        : 2 hour walltime (from --time=2:00:00)
# --setattr=system.memory=17408M : 17GB memory (from --mem=17GB)
# --job-name=brats : job name (from --job-name=brats)
# --output=logs/test_brats.txt : stdout/stderr redirection (from --output=logs/test_brats.txt)
#
# Note: Flux uses -g for GPU count, specific GPU types cannot be requested in standard syntax
# Note: Memory specification syntax: 17GB = 17408MB (17 * 1024)
# Alternative memory syntax: --setattr=system.memory=17G (if supported by Flux version)

# Original job name: brats
# Set at submission: flux batch --job-name=brats ...

# Original output file: logs/test_brats.txt
# Set at submission: flux batch --output=logs/test_brats.txt ...
# Note: Flux combines stdout and stderr to the same file by default
# To separate: add --error=logs/test_brats.err

# Email notification: (empty email address)
# Original: --mail-user= --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL
# Note: Flux does not have built-in email notification directives
# Performance impact: User must manually monitor job status or implement external
# monitoring solutions using flux job events, flux watch commands, or wrapper scripts
# Consider using flux job attach with notifications or external monitoring tools
# Email events: BEGIN, END, FAIL would need custom implementation

# GPU allocation: 1 GPU
# Note: The original Slurm script uses --gres=gpu:1 (generic GPU request)
# Flux uses -g 1 for GPU count allocation
# GPU type/model cannot be specified in standard Flux syntax
# Performance impact: Job may be allocated any available GPU type
# Consult site-specific Flux configuration for GPU property constraints

# Memory: 17GB
# Note: Flux memory specification may vary by version
# Using --setattr=system.memory=17408M (MB) or =17G (if supported)
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory request, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient and cause OOM errors

# Tasks and cores:
# Original: --ntasks-per-node=4 on --nodes=1 = 4 total tasks
# Flux: -N 1 -n 4 (1 node, 4 tasks total)
# No explicit cores-per-task specified, defaulting to 1 core per task
# If the application needs more cores per task, add -c <cores> to submission

# Directory creation for logs (ensure logs directory exists)
mkdir -p logs

# module load tensorboardx/1.2.0-py36-cuda90 torchvision/0.2.1-py36
# module load intel-mkl/2017.2.174 intel-cc/17.0.2.174 intel-fc/17.0.2.174 caffe/0.16.6
# module load pytorch/1.1.0-py36-cuda90 cuda/9.2.88 gcc/6.4.0 eigen/3.2.9 python/3.6.1 xfce/4.12

python train_brats.py \
--dataset="brats" \
--data_dir="datasets/BraTS"  \
--resume_epoch=-1 \
--test_epoch=-1 \
--optimizer="adam" \
--spatial_size=128 \
--prune_spatial_size=96 \
--enable_cuda \
--width 2 \
--number_of_fmaps 4 \
--neuron_sparsity=0.7817 \
--resource_list_type="grad_flops" \
--enable_train \
--valid_spatial_size=192 \

# --enable_test
# --enable_viz
# --neuron_sparsity=0.7817
# --resume_path="models/brats18/RANP_f/model_epoch197.pth"
# --enable_layer_neuron_display

issues: The script correctly documents that Flux does not support in-script resource directives and provides proper submission command syntax in comments.

The memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory=17408M' may not be correct for all Flux versions. Flux typically does not use the 'system.memory' attribute path. The correct syntax is often just '--setattr=memory=17408M' or resource specification may need different syntax like '-o per-resource.memory=17408M' depending on Flux version. Verify with local Flux documentation.
The GPU allocation syntax '-g 1' is correct for Flux, but availability depends on Flux version and configuration. Some versions may require '-o gpu-per-task=1' or '-o gpus-per-node=1' instead.

The submission command specifies '-n 4' (4 tasks) with '-c 1' (1 core per task) which allocates 4 cores total. However, the Python script uses '--enable_cuda' suggesting GPU workload. Verify if 4 tasks are actually needed or if this should be a single-task GPU job with more cores per task (e.g., '-n 1 -c 4').

The script creates 'logs' directory with 'mkdir -p logs' which is good practice, but this happens after job submission starts. If the output redirection '--output=logs/test_brats.txt' is specified at submission time and the directory doesn't exist, the job may fail before the script runs. Consider creating the directory before submission.

All module load commands are commented out. If these modules are required for the Python environment (PyTorch, CUDA, etc.), the script will fail. Uncomment and verify module availability in Flux environment.
The python command has a trailing backslash after '--valid_spatial_size=192 \' which continues the command but has no following arguments. This is syntactically valid but unusual style.

No validation that the required GPU is actually allocated and visible to the Python process. Consider adding a check like 'nvidia-smi' or checking CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES before running the Python script.
The time limit '-t 2h' may be insufficient for training neural networks on BraTS dataset. Consider if 2 hours is adequate for the training job.

No specification of which task(s) should have GPU access when using 4 tasks. With '-n 4 -g 1', the GPU allocation behavior may be ambiguous. Consider if this should be '-n 1 -c 4 -g 1' for a single multi-threaded task with GPU.
